{{< lead >}}
I copy out the lines **that stay with me**, one at a time, as I find them. Some come with **a painting**; most come with nothing but **the voice that said them**.
{{< /lead >}}

They are **quoted as I published them**, in the language I read them in, which is sometimes Spanish and sometimes English. Nothing here has been **translated, corrected or tidied** — the punctuation inside each quote is the punctuation I typed.

{{< quote-random label="Open at random" >}}

## Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

{{< quote
  cite="Johann Wolfgang von Goethe"
  date="2022-12-12"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1602404246896386050" >}}
"Lo que brilla, ha nacido para el instante; lo auténtico permanece intacto para la posteridad."
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  cite="Mefistófeles en referencia a El Señor. Fausto, J. W. Goethe"
  date="2022-12-12"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1602405711819972609" >}}
"(Solo.) De tiempo en tiempo pláceme ver al Viejo, y me guardo bien de romper con él. Muy linda cosa es, por parte de todo un gran señor, el hablar tan humanamente con el mismo diablo."
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  cite="Mefistófeles en respuesta a ¿quien eres tú?. Fausto, J. W. Goethe"
  date="2022-12-12"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1602409615689453570" >}}
"Una parte de aquel poder que siempre quiere el mal y siempre produce el bien."
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  cite="Mefistófeles. Fausto, J. W. Goethe"
  date="2022-12-12"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1602413319901839360" >}}
"Es ley para diablos y espectros, que por donde se colaron, por allí han de salir. Lo primero es libre para nosotros; de lo segundo somos esclavos."
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  cite="Johann Wolfgang von Goethe"
  date="2022-12-12"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1602416836729004032" >}}
"Soy demasiado viejo para andar en juegos, y demasiado joven para estar sin deseos."
{{< /quote >}}

## Jorge Luis Borges

{{< quote
  cite="Fragmentos de un evangelio apócrifo, Jorge Luis Borges"
  date="2022-12-12"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1602446480077651968" >}}
"27. Yo no hablo de venganzas ni de perdones; el olvido es la única venganza y el único perdón."
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  cite="Epílogo de El hacedor, Jorge Luis Borges"
  date="2022-12-14"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1603147630556635141" >}}
"Un hombre se propone la tarea de dibujar el mundo. A lo largo de los años puebla un espacio con imágenes de provincias, de reinos, de montañas, de bahías, de naves, de islas, de peces, de habitaciones, de instrumentos, de astros, de caballos y de personas. Poco antes de morir, descubre que ese paciente laberinto de líneas traza la imagen de su cara."
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  cite="Fragmentos de un evangelio apócrifo, Jorge Luis Borges"
  date="2022-12-14"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1603151934319661057" >}}
"39. Busca por el agrado de buscar, no por el de encontrar... "
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  cite="Jorge Luis Borges, El Aleph"
  date="2024-04-01"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1774765264267030919" >}}
"Ser inmortal es baladí; menos el hombre, todas las criaturas lo son, pues ignoran la muerte; lo divino, lo terrible, lo incomprensible, es saberse inmortal."
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  cite="Fragmentos de un evangelio apócrifo, Jorge Luis Borges"
  date="2024-08-31"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1829785352912896375" >}}
"7. Feliz el que no insiste en tener razón, porque nadie la tiene o todos la tienen."
{{< /quote >}}

## Juan Rulfo

{{< quote
  cite="Juan Rulfo, Cartas a Clara"
  date="2022-12-24"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1606558999574355969" >}}
"Ese sueño que eres tú todavía dura. Durará siempre, porque siento como que estás dentro de mi sangre y pasas por mi corazón a cada rato."
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  cite="Juan Rulfo, Cartas a Clara"
  date="2022-12-24"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1606560083730735104" >}}
"Estas pláticas que yo tengo con mi conciencia son a veces muy largas, duran días enteros; por eso no resulta que me ponga a contártelas en esta pobre carta. De verdad, cuídate mucho, come y duerme bien y sueña con los angelitos y no en esta cosa maligna que soy yo. Pero no me olvides."
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  cite="Pedro Paramo, Juan Rulfo"
  date="2023-04-21"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1649300134042189826"
  image="img/sorolla-1909-the-wounded-foot.jpg"
  alt="Two children crouching in shallow sunlit water, one tending the other's foot"
  credit="Sorolla, J. (1909). The Wounded Foot." >}}
«El día que te fuiste entendí que no te volvería a ver. Ibas teñida de rojo
por el sol de la tarde, por el crepúsculo ensangrentado del cielo. Sonreías»
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  cite="Pedro Paramo, Juan Rulfo"
  date="2023-04-21"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1649300144347660288"
  image="img/sorolla-1908-sea-idyll.jpg"
  alt="Two young figures lying in clear shallow water, seen from above"
  credit="Sorolla, J. (1908). Sea Idyll." >}}
«Dejabas atrás un pueblo del que muchas veces me dijiste: “Lo quiero por ti; pero lo odio por todo lo demás, hasta por haber nacido en él”. Pensé: “No regresará jamás; no volverá nunca”»
{{< /quote >}}

## José Ángel Buesa

The whole of *Poema del olvido*, in three parts, each read against a painting by Winslow Homer.

{{< quote
  cite="Poema del olvido, José Ángel Buesa"
  date="2023-03-29"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1641278979142189061"
  image="img/homer-1890-summer-night.jpg"
  alt="Two women dancing together on a shore at night while onlookers watch the moonlit surf"
  credit="Homer, W. (1890). Summer night." >}}
"y hoy tu vida y mi vida son como estrellas,
pues pueden verse juntas, estando tan lejanas..."
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  cite="Poema del olvido, José Ángel Buesa"
  date="2023-03-29"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1641278985622503425"
  image="img/homer-1885-lost-on-the-grand-banks.jpg"
  alt="Two fishermen in a small dory on heavy grey seas, straining to see through the fog"
  credit="Homer, W. (1885). Lost on the Grand Banks." >}}
"Yo bien sé que el olvido, como un agua maldita,
nos da una sed más honda que la sed que nos quita,
pero estoy tan seguro de poder olvidar..."
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  cite="Poema del olvido, José Ángel Buesa"
  date="2023-03-29"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1641278996431220739"
  image="img/homer-1909-driftwood.jpg"
  alt="A lone figure in dark oilskins on wet rocks beside a breaking wave"
  credit="Homer, W. (1909). Driftwood." >}}
"Y miraré las nubes sin pensar que te quiero,
con el hábito sordo de un viejo marinero
que aún siente, en tierra firme, la ondulación del mar."
{{< /quote >}}

## Yann Martel

{{< quote
  cite="Life of Pi, Yann Martel"
  date="2023-04-06"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1643892449259970564"
  image="img/delacroix-1862-tiger-and-snake.jpg"
  alt="A tiger crouching low, snarling at a snake coiled around a tree trunk"
  credit="Delacroix, E. (1862). Tiger and Snake." >}}
"I've never forgotten him. Dare I say I miss him? I do. I miss him. I still see him in my dreams. They are nightmares mostly, but nightmares tinged with love."
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  cite="Life of Pi, Yann Martel"
  date="2023-04-06"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1643892461738119168"
  image="img/delacroix-1830-tiger.jpg"
  alt="A watercolour of a tiger lying curled on open ground before blue mountains"
  credit="Delacroix, E. (1830). Tiger." >}}
"Such is the strangeness of the human heart. I still cannot understand how he could abandon me so unceremoniously, without any sort of goodbye, without looking back even once."
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  cite="Life of Pi, Yann Martel"
  date="2023-04-07"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1644473138825027589"
  image="img/schiele-1917-the-embrace.jpg"
  alt="Two figures lying on a white sheet, holding each other, painted in heavy ochre and flesh tones"
  credit="Schiele, E. (1917). The Embrace." >}}
"I suppose in the end, the whole of life becomes an act of letting go, but what always hurts the most is not taking a moment to say goodbye."
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  cite="Life of Pi, Yann Martel"
  date="2023-04-08"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1644923186864062464"
  image="img/homer-the-water-fan.jpg"
  alt="A man leaning out of a small boat over calm blue water, looking down through a glass-bottomed bucket"
  credit="The water fan." >}}
"What a terrible thing it is to botch a farewell. I am a person who believes in form, in the harmony of order.
Where we can, we must give things a meaningful shape."
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  cite="Life of Pi, Yann Martel"
  date="2023-04-08"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1644923197282832385"
  image="img/homer-the-gulf-stream.jpg"
  alt="A man lying on the deck of a dismasted boat in a heavy sea, sharks circling around it"
  credit="The Gulf Stream." >}}
"It's important in life to conclude things properly. Only then can you let go. Otherwise you are left with words you should have said but never did, and your heart is heavy with remorse.
That bungled goodbye hurts me to this day."
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  cite="Life of Pi, Yann Martel"
  date="2023-04-08"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1644923212025700354"
  image="img/homer-after-the-hurricane.jpg"
  alt="A man lying face down on a beach beside his wrecked boat, under a dark sky"
  credit="After the Hurricane." >}}
"I wish you all the best with it. Watch out for Man. He is not your friend. But I hope you will remember me as a friend. I will never forget you , that is certain.
You will always be with me, in my heart."
{{< /quote >}}

## Takehiko Inoue

{{< quote
  cite="Takehiko Inoue"
  date="2024-08-25"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1827642278606688455"
  image="img/inoue-vagabond-musashi.jpg"

## Gabriel García Márquez

{{< quote
  cite="Cien años de soledad, Gabriel García Márquez"
  date="2025-11-28" >}}
"Aureliano Segundo pensaba sin decirlo que el mal no estaba en el mundo, sino en algún lugar recóndito del misterioso corazón de Petra Cotes, donde algo había ocurrido durante el diluvio que volvió estériles a los animales y escurridizo el dinero. Intrigado con ese enigma, escarbó tan profundamente en los sentimientos de ella, que buscando el interés encontró el amor porque tratando de que ella lo quisiera terminó por quererla. Petra Cotes, por su parte, lo iba queriendo más a medida que sentía aumentar su cariño, y fue así como en la plenitud del otoño volvió a creer en la superstición juvenil de que la pobreza era una servidumbre del amor"
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  cite="John Williams, Stoner"
  date="2024-04-01"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1774752632675921929" >}}
"In his extreme youth Stoner had thought of love as an absolute state of being to which, if one were lucky, one might find access; ... in his maturity he had decided it was the heaven of a false religion, toward which one ought to gaze with an amused disbelief, a gently familiar contempt, and an embarrassed nostalgia. ... Now in his middle age he began to know that it was neither a state of grace nor an illusion; he saw it as a human act of becoming, a condition that was invented and modified moment by moment and day by day, by the will and the intelligence and the heart."

  date="2024-10-22"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1848655971456848177" >}}
«Una sola cosa importa: aprender a ser perdedor»
{{< /quote >}}

---

## Aphorisms

They are not quotations of anyone: they are the short forms a language keeps because they say in three words something it would otherwise take a paragraph to say. Under each one is what I went and found out about it.

{{< quote
  note="Japanese, 物の哀れ — “the pathos of things”. Not sadness at things but the ache of noticing that they pass: the cherry blossom is moving *because* it falls. Named by the scholar Motoori Norinaga in the eighteenth century, reading the Genji."
  date="2023-01-03"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1610199841736368132" >}}
Mono no aware
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  note="Latin, “remember that you must die”. Roman, and later carried into Christian painting as the skull set beside the books: not a threat, a measure. Whatever you are weighing, weigh it against this."
  date="2023-01-03"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1610201048643428352" >}}
Memento mori
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  note="Latin, “time flees”. From Virgil's Georgics, where the full line is *fugit irreparabile tempus* — it flees, and it cannot be recovered. The second half is the one that bites."
  date="2023-01-03"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1610202456398467072" >}}
Tempus fugit
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  note="Latin, “seize the day”. Horace, Odes I.11, and the rest of the line is usually dropped: *carpe diem, quam minimum credula postero* — seize the day, trusting tomorrow as little as you can. *Carpere* is what you do to fruit, not to a prize."
  date="2023-01-03"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1610202769020837890" >}}
Carpe diem
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  note="Latin, “art is long, life is short”. Hippocrates wrote it first in Greek and meant it of medicine: the craft takes longer to learn than a lifetime gives you. The common reading, that art outlives the artist, reverses which of the two is the problem."
  date="2023-01-03"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1610207756392210432" >}}
Ars longa, vita brevis
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  note="Latin, “the golden mean”. Horace again, Odes II.10: the one who loves it keeps clear both of a hovel and of a palace worth envying. It argues for the middle not as timidity but as the only place that is not exposed."
  date="2023-01-03"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1610208578186661890" >}}
Aurea mediocritas
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  note="Latin, “by teaching, we learn”. From a letter of Seneca: *homines dum docent discunt* — while they teach, people learn. Anyone who has had to explain something they thought they knew has met this one."
  date="2023-01-03"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1610211846312820739" >}}
Docendo discimus
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  note="Latin, “dare to know”. Horace, taken up by Kant in 1784 as the motto of the Enlightenment, where he glossed it: have the courage to use your own understanding. The dare is the point; the knowing was never the hard part."
  date="2023-01-03"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1610214149862170626" >}}
Sapere aude
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  note="Latin, “if you want peace, prepare for war”. Adapted from Vegetius, a late Roman writer on military matters. It has been used ever since to justify both restraint and armament, which is a fair measure of how much it actually settles."
  date="2023-01-03"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1610215075515883524" >}}
Si vis pacem, para bellum
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  note="Latin, “the truth shall set you free”. John 8:32, in the Vulgate. It is carved over the entrances of a great many universities, usually without the clause before it, which makes the freedom conditional on staying in the word."
  date="2023-01-03"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1610215895808221185" >}}
Veritas vos liberabit
{{< /quote >}}

{{< quote
  note="From *Silver Linings Playbook*, where Pat writes the word on a sheet of paper and tapes it to the wall. *Excelsior* is Latin for *ever upward*, and in the film it is the rule he gives himself: to keep looking for the silver lining in whatever happens. Pat Sr.’s speech from the same film is in [Cinema](/spaces/cinema/#favorite-drama-film)."
  date="2023-06-27"
  url="https://x.com/dafmontenegro/status/1673857183329529859"
  image="img/silver-linings-playbook-excelsior.jpg"
  alt="A sheet of paper taped to a tiled wall with EXCELSIOR written across it by hand"
  image2="img/silver-linings-playbook-pat.jpg"
  alt2="Pat in close-up, looking straight down the lens, in the scene the film opens with"
  credit="Silver Linings Playbook (2012)." >}}
¡Excelsior!
{{< /quote >}}
